summary: Inspect the supplied evidence and distinguish what each check establishes.

blocks.text: A declared-versus-current difference is evidence within a limited comparison scope.
Drift detection compares current values with supported resource properties explicitly declared in CloudFormation.
After the supplied out-of-band change, run detection on the provisioned stack, wait for completion, and inspect the bucket’s expected/actual property pair.
Detection reports differences but does not repair them. Unsupported or undeclared properties may not be checked.

steps.title: Work through the evidence: Observe CloudFormation drift

blocks.text: Record the checked bucket property as supplied declared value A versus current value B. Wait for completed detection before interpreting the pair. Keep the supported, explicitly declared comparison scope beside it. A missing report for another property does not establish that property’s correctness, and detection alone makes no repair.
Detection is neither correction nor exhaustive checking of every property. Unsupported or undeclared properties may fall outside the comparison.

buckets.label: Meets the stated criterion / conclusion supported
Does not meet the criterion / conclusion unsupported

items.text:
Provisioning record identifies the supplied stack bucket. After supplied out-of-band change, detection completes. Stack resource and supported explicitly declared property recorded: expected declared value A, actual current value B.
Conclusion: this checked property differs; detection has not repaired it and does not establish correctness of unsupported or undeclared properties.

Provisioned bucket; completed detection. Checked property expected A, actual B.
Conclusion: detection repaired B back to A.

Provisioned bucket; completed detection. Checked supported property expected A, actual B.
Conclusion: every unsupported and undeclared property is now verified correct.

i1.message: The resource, completed check and expected/actual pair support only the bounded difference and stated limitations.

i2.message: Detection reports differences without repair; the actual B observation does not establish restoration to A.

i3.message: The supported explicitly declared property comparison does not establish correctness of unsupported or undeclared properties.

correct.message: Each judgement follows the supplied excerpt and the verification criterion.

incorrect.message: Check the evidence behind each conclusion; a partial success does not establish every required boundary.

hints: Look for the exact expected/current pair and the limits of the check.

steps.title: Read update failure and rollback separately

blocks.text: The original update failure and the rollback outcome are separate evidence.
CloudFormation stack events record resource operation status and failure reasons during updates.
For the supplied controlled update failure, inspect the first failing resource event, then the subsequent rollback events.
UPDATE_ROLLBACK_COMPLETE means rollback to the previous working stack state. UPDATE_ROLLBACK_FAILED requires resolving the rollback failure before continuing.

steps.title: Work through the evidence: Read update failure and rollback separately

blocks.text: Read the first failing resource and its reason, then follow rollback events. Keep the original failure separate from a later rollback failure. UPDATE_ROLLBACK_COMPLETE describes restoration of the previous working state; UPDATE_ROLLBACK_FAILED leaves a rollback failure to resolve before continuing through the approved response path.
UPDATE_ROLLBACK_FAILED is not rollback success. UPDATE_ROLLBACK_COMPLETE is not successful deployment of the failed update.

steps.title: Check read update failure and rollback separately
steps.lede: Read the supplied evidence in this step and choose the interpretation it supports.

public.prompt: Two supplied update sequences finish with UPDATE_ROLLBACK_COMPLETE and UPDATE_ROLLBACK_FAILED respectively. Which interpretation is correct?

options.text: The completed status means the failed update’s desired change is now deployed.
The first returned to the previous working stack state; the second requires resolving rollback failure before continuing.
Both statuses mean rollback completed successfully.

o1.message: Completed rollback indicates the previous working state, not success of the failed update.

o2.message: This follows the stated evidence and the taught verification rule.

o3.message: UPDATE_ROLLBACK_FAILED is not completed rollback and requires resolution.

correct.message: Your choice follows the stated evidence and verification rule.

incorrect.message: Recheck the evidence and the explanation for the selected option.

items.text:
Initial stack: one EC2 instance provisioned. Controlled update: first failing resource event identifies the supplied EC2 resource and supplied failure reason. Later rollback events end UPDATE_ROLLBACK_COMPLETE.
Report: first failure/reason recorded separately; terminal status confirms return to the previous working stack state.

Initial stack: one EC2 instance provisioned. First update failure and its reason recorded. Subsequent rollback events end UPDATE_ROLLBACK_FAILED.
Report: routine continuation stopped; resolve rollback failure through established guidance before continuing.

Initial stack: one EC2 instance provisioned. First update failure recorded; later rollback event fails and terminal status is UPDATE_ROLLBACK_FAILED.
Report: use the later rollback failure as the original update cause and proceed because rollback completed.

i1.message: The original update failure is separated from rollback evidence and COMPLETE is interpreted as return to the previous working state.

i2.message: FAILED requires rollback-failure resolution before continuation, not a completed-state claim.

i3.message: The first update failure is distinct from the later rollback failure, and FAILED does not confirm completed rollback.

correct.message: Each judgement follows the supplied excerpt and the verification criterion.

incorrect.message: Check the evidence behind each conclusion; a partial success does not establish every required boundary.

hints: Separate the first update failure from later rollback events and terminal status.
